item.title: Statement by Prime Minister Carney on the 30th anniversary of the final report of the Royal Commission on Aboriginal Peoples
item.description:
“Thirty years ago, the Royal Commission on Aboriginal Peoples (RCAP) released its landmark final report – a roadmap for repairing the relationship between Indigenous Peoples and Canada. After visiting Indigenous communities across the country and hearing from more than 2,000 individuals through public hearings, the Commission put forward 440 recommendations to address generations of injustice and to build a new relationship grounded in recognition, respect, and partnership.

The Commission’s message was clear: First Nations, Inuit, and Métis have the inherent right to govern themselves, preserve their languages and cultures, and determine their own futures. Canada has a responsibility to recognise those rights, honour treaties, and build relationships grounded in mutual respect and partnership.

The report helped lay the foundation for decades of work toward reconciliation, including the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action, the Calls for Justice of the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls, and the implementation of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act.

The Commission’s recommendations helped shape the work of successive governments to recognise Indigenous self-government, renew treaty relationships, and create economic development opportunities while improving access to education, housing, and infrastructure. Today, that work continues in true partnership with Indigenous Peoples, ensuring that First Nations, Inuit, and Métis have a share in the prosperity we create together.

Thirty years on, the Commission’s vision remains unfinished. Reconciliation is not the work of one report, one government, or one generation. It is a responsibility we must carry forward, together.”

item.title: Prime Minister Carney meets with Prime Minister of Singapore Lawrence Wong, Prime Minister of Australia Anthony Albanese, and Prime Minister of New Zealand Christopher Luxon
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, met with the Prime Minister of Singapore, Lawrence Wong, the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese, and the Prime Minister of New Zealand, Christopher Luxon, on the margins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China.

The leaders underscored the close partnership among their countries, with Canada's combined merchandise trade with Singapore, Australia, and New Zealand exceeding $15 billion in 2025. They discussed ways to build on these strong commercial ties and expand trade and investment, including through the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) – a trading bloc of 580 million consumers and 15.6% of global GDP.

In a more fragmented global economy, the prime ministers reaffirmed their shared commitment to open and predictable markets and a rules-based international trading system. They discussed the importance of closer cooperation among trusted partners to build more resilient supply chains, bolster AI governance, and strengthen our collective economic security. The leaders also agreed to deepen defence and security cooperation to advance peace, stability, and prosperity across the Indo-Pacific.

The prime ministers agreed to advance these shared priorities and remain in close contact.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney strengthens economic partnerships at APEC, capping an ambitious week that delivered major gains for Canadian workers and businesses
item.description:
Canada is moving strategically, pragmatically, and decisively to secure greater access to new markets and attract new investment – building our strength at home and diversifying our partnerships abroad.

To these ends, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, represented Canada this week at the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China. There, APEC leaders outlined a shared vision for the Asia-Pacific to remain the world’s most dynamic and interconnected region. Prime Minister Carney emphasised the importance of predictable trade, resilient supply chains, and deeper economic integration in driving investment, innovation, and shared prosperity across the region.

At the Summit, the leaders renewed APEC’s Connectivity Blueprint to strengthen the infrastructure and supply chains that move our goods, advanced paperless trade to cut costs for businesses, and agreed on common principles to protect food supplies from global disruptions. Prime Minister Carney highlighted how Canada is leading this work at home: fast-tracking major projects, including doubling the capacity of the Port of Vancouver and building a pipeline to the West Coast, and introducing digital trade legislation through the Canada Strong Act.

On the margins of the Summit, the Prime Minister met with the leaders of Australia, China, Mexico, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Thailand, and the United States. He advanced partnerships that will strengthen economic competitiveness, connectivity, and resilience, highlighting Canada’s world-class capabilities in artificial intelligence, critical minerals, energy, and financial technology.

The APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting capped an ambitious week-long trip across Europe and Asia, during which Prime Minister Carney advanced landmark trade agreements, strengthened Canada’s economic and security partnerships, and mobilised Canadian expertise and capital to address global challenges:

  • In Dublin, Ireland, Prime Minister Carney attended the Summit of the European Political Community and advanced Canada and the European Union’s (EU) joint mission to forge the closest possible partnership, short of Canada joining the EU. Building on the Alliance for the Future launched in Montréal last month, he advanced cooperation with European leaders to open new markets, strengthen supply chains, and reinforce collective defence. He also reaffirmed Canada’s unwavering support for Ukraine.
  • In Manila, Philippines, Prime Minister Carney announced the substantial conclusion of negotiations toward an ASEAN-Canada free trade agreement and the conclusion of negotiations on a Canada-Philippines free trade agreement, with the ambition of signing both in 2027. The agreement with ASEAN will open greater access to a market of nearly 700 million people, and alone is expected to add nearly $2 billion to Canada’s GDP and create nearly 14,000 Canadian jobs, while the agreement with the Philippines could triple Canadian exports to the country by 2035. The Prime Minister also strengthened Canada’s defence and security partnership with the Philippines, and announced Canada’s landmark contribution of up to $560 million to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility to help mobilise private investment for climate and nature action.
  • In Phnom Penh, Cambodia, Prime Minister Carney strengthened Canada’s partnerships across La Francophonie and welcomed Canada’s designation as host of the 2028 Sommet de la Francophonie. The Summit will bring together delegates from more than 90 states and governments in the National Capital Region to deepen economic and cultural ties and advance the protection of the French language in the digital age. The Prime Minister also advanced Canada’s bilateral relationship with Cambodia, announcing new initiatives on trade, investment, defence, and security.
  • In Shenzhen, China, Prime Minister Carney delivered further gains under the Canada-China strategic partnership. With an extension and expansion of the bilateral economic and trade arrangement until December 2028 that will provide additional tariff relief for approximately $400 million in Canadian exports, Canada has now restored market access for more than 90% of trade previously subject to tariff action – nearly $7.5 billion worth of Canadian exports. The Prime Minister also announced a Canada-China Year of e-Commerce and a major trade mission to China, both in 2027, and welcomed new commercial and technical agreements and investments in education, business, financial services, and the arts and culture sector, expanding the reach of Canadian businesses in one of the world’s largest markets.

Canada has the resources, the talent, and the capital the world needs. Throughout his engagements, the Prime Minister brought these strengths to new markets and new partnerships with the speed, ambition, and scale that this moment demands. With 20 free trade agreements across 60 countries, Canada will have preferential access to more than 2 billion consumers, representing two-thirds of global GDP – making Canada the best-connected economy in the world. And Canada is just getting started.

Quote

“Sovereignty is built on strength at home and diverse partnerships abroad. Everything we achieved this week – two new free trade agreements, expanded trade with China, stronger ties across Asia and Europe – reinforces that goal. Canada is now the best-connected economy in the world, and we are just getting started – so we can live our lives as we choose.”

The Rt. Hon. Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada

Quick facts

  • In Shenzhen, Prime Minister Carney was joined by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Anita Anand.
  • In 2025, APEC’s 21 member economies accounted for more than 61% of global GDP and 80.6% of Canada’s merchandise trade. Canada has free trade agreements with 12 APEC economies.
  • As Canada and China elevate their strategic partnership, the Government of Canada earlier this week approved the application of the Agricultural Bank of China to establish a full-service branch in Canada.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney meets with President of Mexico Claudia Sheinbaum
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, met with the President of Mexico, Claudia Sheinbaum, on the margins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China.

Prime Minister Carney and President Sheinbaum reaffirmed their commitment to renewing the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA).

The leaders highlighted the first anniversary of the Canada-Mexico Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, launched during the Prime Minister’s visit to Mexico last year, and welcomed significant progress in its implementation through the Canada-Mexico Action Plan, with more than 130 initiatives launched over the past year across its four pillars.

Prime Minister Carney and President Sheinbaum underscored the growing strength of the bilateral economic relationship, with merchandise trade up 19% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period last year. They welcomed nearly $1 billion in Mexican investments in Canadian mining and food production and over $3.7 billion in Canadian investments in Mexico’s manufacturing, renewable energy, and mining sectors. The leaders also highlighted expanded market access for Canadian agricultural and agri-food products and the success of trade missions in both countries, which together generated more than 3,700 business-to-business meetings and more than 100 commercial agreements and new partnerships. They emphasised the potential for further growth in advanced manufacturing, agriculture, critical minerals, energy, pharmaceuticals, and transportation.

The Prime Minister and the President welcomed progress in strengthening bilateral security cooperation, including through a new Strategic Security Dialogue, close to 30 key stakeholder engagements and training exercises, and over $10 million for security capacity and cooperation initiatives. They highlighted closer cooperation on environmental stewardship, as well as joint initiatives to advance health security, biomanufacturing, labour mobility, and Indigenous prosperity.

Building on this progress, the leaders agreed to accelerate the implementation of the Action Plan in its second year, with a focus on building resilient and competitive supply chains, expanding bilateral trade and investment, and deepening security cooperation to deliver tangible benefits for Canadians and Mexicans. The two leaders expressed a desire to identify further areas of cooperation, including in critical minerals, defence, and partnerships in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond.

Prime Minister Carney and President Sheinbaum agreed to remain in close contact.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney meets with President of the People’s Republic of China Xi Jinping
item.description:
Today, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, met with the President of the People’s Republic of China, Xi Jinping, during his visit to Shenzhen, China.

Prime Minister Carney and President Xi agreed that the Canada-China strategic partnership is working successfully. It is increasing mutually beneficial two-way trade, generating new business investment between our countries, and strengthening people-to-people ties.

The leaders focused on how to further elevate this partnership. To that end, they welcomed the extension of the current trade arrangement and agreed to expand it to reduce tariffs on more items, including most frozen pork cuts, Greenland halibut, certain shrimps including Pacific spot prawns, certain molluscs including geoduck and sea cucumbers. Over 90% of Canada-China trade is now on reduced tariffs.

Prime Minister Carney and President Xi highlighted the strong ties between their peoples. They welcomed new commercial agreements and partnerships between Canadian and Chinese businesses and institutions, including in the arts, culture, and education sectors. The leaders agreed that the peoples of both countries are benefitting from these renewed ties between Canada and China, including an increase in two-way tourism. They noted the expansion of direct air services between the two countries, making it easier for Canadians and Chinese citizens to travel, study, and do business.

The Prime Minister and the President discussed the outcomes of the Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue, which included closer engagement between the two countries’ financial, monetary, and regulatory authorities. They agreed to expand trade in services and highlighted improved access to education and financial services. They also exchanged views on developments in the global economy and financial systems.

The leaders each outlined opportunities to deepen cooperation in clean and conventional energy industries, including oil and gas, low-carbon technologies, and electric vehicles. They underscored the importance of maintaining open channels of communication on security issues and emphasised the ongoing importance for border and customs cooperation to combat illicit drug trafficking.

Prime Minister Carney and President Xi agreed on the importance of strengthening cooperation on the global governance of artificial intelligence (AI), recognising both the transformative potential of AI and the need to address its risks. They emphasised the urgency of working together to promote the safe and responsible development and use of AI, including through greater international cooperation and dialogue.

The leaders reaffirmed their commitment to deepening cooperation in multilateral fora, including the United Nations. They discussed the deepening cooperation under the Kunming Dialogue and their shared commitment to sustainable growth. Prime Minister Carney announced that Canada will renew its long-standing support to the China Council on International Cooperation on Environment and Development for the next five years.

Prime Minister Carney thanked President Xi for China’s leadership in hosting this year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The leaders welcomed Prime Minister Carney’s visit as an important step forward in strengthening the Canada-China relationship and building a more constructive partnership that delivers lasting benefits for both countries and their peoples. They agreed to remain in close contact.

item.title: Prime Minister Carney advances Canada’s strategic partnership with China across trade, commerce, and culture
item.description:
Over the past year and a half, Canada’s government has recalibrated our relationship with China – strategically, pragmatically, and decisively. Last January, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, and the President of the People’s Republic of China, Xi Jinping, launched a new Canada-China strategic partnership to stabilise trade, build out clean energy industries, and better connect our peoples. Under the partnership, Canada and China have strengthened economic and financial cooperation, expanded cultural exchanges, and reduced tariffs on Canadian exports of canola seed and meal, peas, crab, and lobster. To date, Canada has restored market access for more than 90% of trade previously subject to tariff action – nearly $7.5 billion worth of Canadian exports.

To build on that success, Prime Minister Carney today met with President Xi in Shenzhen, China. The leaders agreed on new measures that will further expand trade between their two countries.

Canada and China are announcing:

  • An extension and expansion of the Preliminary Joint Arrangement on Addressing Bilateral Economic and Trade Issues between Canada and China. This will further improve access to the Chinese market for Canada’s farmers and seafood harvesters and provide additional tariff relief for approximately $400 million in Canadian exports, including $116 million in exports of frozen pork cuts and $285 million in fish and seafood exports, covering certain frozen cold-water shrimp and prawns, including Pacific spot prawn; certain molluscs, including geoduck; sea cucumber; and Greenland halibut.
    • The expansion builds on the two-year extension of tariff relief for Canadian exports of canola meal, peas, lobster, and crab announced earlier this month.
    • In exchange, Canada has agreed to extend by two years existing remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products that are currently set to expire at the end of 2026, and to expand remissions coverage to an additional 32 steel and aluminium tariff items for which Canadian supply is insufficient or unavailable.

To create more opportunities for investment, education, and exchanges between our countries, Prime Minister Carney announced:

  • The endorsement of Joint Outcomes from the 2nd Canada-China Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue to strengthen bilateral economic, trade, and financial relations, including through practical cooperation between financial and macroeconomic, regulatory, and monetary authorities from both countries.
  • A new major trade mission to China in 2027 to connect Canadian businesses with key Chinese industry leaders.
  • A Canada-China Year of e-Commerce in 2027 – a practical initiative that will help Canadian small and medium-sized enterprises compete, diversify, and grow via Chinese e-commerce platforms.
  • A Canadian contribution of $850,000 for scholarships under the Canada Learning Initiative in China to enable 850 Canadian students to study at Chinese universities.
  • A Canadian contribution of $8 million to the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development to mobilise international expertise on environmental issues, including from Canadian researchers, and make science-based recommendations to policymakers.

The expanded partnership between Canada and China is also at play in the private sector. During the visit, Prime Minister Carney and President Xi welcomed the following agreements and investments from businesses:

  • New air routes between Canada and China, with Air Canada launching new flights from Vancouver to Guangzhou in May 2027 and Chinese airlines also increasing flights.
  • Over $15 million worth of commercial agreements signed by five Canadian companies from the arts and culture sector.
  • A memorandum of understanding (MOU) to launch a Canada-China CEO Roundtable. Co-chaired by the Canada-China Business Council and the Bank of China, this initiative will provide a forum for enhanced business-to-business exchanges between the two countries.
  • A MOU between the University of Ottawa (uOttawa) and the Shanghai International Studies University (SISU) to develop an undergraduate dual-degree program combining uOttawa’s expertise in international studies and modern languages with SISU’s research strengths in French studies and diplomacy.

The leaders also discussed the positive outcomes of recent dialogues between Canada and China to increase border and customs cooperation against narcotics threats, and to enhance collaboration on oil and gas, renewable energy, and nuclear with key industry leaders from the energy sector.

As the world’s second-largest economy and a country of more than 1.4 billion people, China plays a central role in Canada’s engagement in the Indo-Pacific. Across Canada, hundreds of thousands of jobs are supported by trade with China – from farmers in the Prairies to manufacturers in Ontario and Québec and fish harvesters in Atlantic Canada and British Columbia. Our trade with China generates over $30 billion in revenues and adds $6.9 billion to Canada’s GDP. By expanding Canada’s access to one of the world’s largest markets, we are opening new avenues for commercial, scientific, and cultural collaboration, and strengthening the ties between our peoples.

In Shenzhen, Prime Minister Carney will represent Canada at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ Meeting to further deepen our partnerships across the region.

Quote

“Canada and China have recalibrated our relationship to the benefit of citizens in both countries. We have unlocked billions in new export orders for Canadian farmers, ranchers, and fish harvesters – for workers and businesses across the country. We’re making it easier to travel, study, and do business between our nations to create more opportunity and prosperity for all. Canada is building our strength at home and diversifying our relationships abroad so that we have the freedom to live our lives as we choose.”

The Rt. Hon. Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada

Quick facts

  • Prime Minister Carney is joined in Shenzhen by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Anita Anand, and the Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister, Kody Blois.
  • In 2025, Canada’s bilateral trade in merchandise with China reached $125.6 billion – a 5.6% increase compared to 2024.
  • China is a key commercial market for Canadian businesses, accounting for $35.1 billion of Canada’s merchandise exports in 2025.
  • In 2025, China’s foreign direct investment (FDI) stock stood at $43.4 billion, ranking China as the fourth-largest investor country in Canada. FDI stock in China from Canada (CDIA) stood at $15 billion, ranking China as the 19th largest destination for CDIA.
